slides.text:
Kevin Martin.

Not from the soundsystem.
Not from the rave.

He came from industrial noise
and metal and dub and jazz.

An outsider who went deeper
than anyone born inside.
slides.image_concept: Abandoned factory or industrial site at night, silhouette of structure against dark sky with distant London skyline, black and white or cold dark tones.
slides.image_keywords: abandoned factory night industrial dark silhouette london skyline

slides.text:
1987. God.
Martin + Justin Broadrick (Godflesh).
Metal. Dub. Free jazz.

1990. Techno Animal.
Industrial + ambient + hip-hop + dub.
Six albums. The obsession deepens.

2001. The Brotherhood of the Bomb.
Their last record together.

For now.
slides.image_concept: Analog synthesizers and tangled cables in a dark studio, single dim lamp, vintage equipment aesthetic.
slides.image_keywords: analog synthesizer tangled cables dark studio vintage

slides.text:
1997. The Bug is born.

Pressure (2003) — Rephlex Records.
Aphex Twin's label.

Dancehall vocals.
Grime edges.
Industrial bass.

London was paying attention.
slides.image_concept: Close-up of vinyl record grooves under a single beam of light against a black background, sharp and minimal.
slides.image_keywords: vinyl record close up grooves dark light black

slides.text:
London Zoo. 2008. Ninja Tune.

37 million CCTV cameras.
The most surveilled city on earth.

Every corner watched.
Every corner afraid.

This album was its sound.
slides.image_concept: London street intersection at night in the rain, CCTV cameras pointing in multiple directions, wet asphalt reflecting orange light, nobody visible.
slides.image_keywords: london street corner CCTV rain night asphalt orange

slides.text:
The voices of London Zoo:

Flowdan (Roll Deep — grime).
Warrior Queen (reggae/dancehall).
Tippa Irie — "Jah War."
Spaceape. Riko Dan. Killa P.

Every voice carried a different London.
Martin gave them all the same bass.
slides.image_concept: Dark recording studio, a single microphone lit by a red talkback light, silhouette of a figure leaning into it.
slides.image_keywords: recording studio microphone silhouette dark red light

slides.text:
The Wire: Record of the Year. 2008.
Metacritic: 90/100.

"Skeng." "Angry." "Jah War."

Not dubstep. Not grime. Not dancehall.

It was what happens
when all three
run out of oxygen.

slides.text:
Music this heavy
does not ask you to listen.

It demands you survive it.

Save this.
